storyboard.claim: The pioneers invented an entire field.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An inventor with a lightbulb: the spark that founded a new field.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the medical-field story from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the invention concrete as a person and a spark, before the narrator turns to the cost.
storyboard.staging: Inventor celebrating beside a lightbulb: the idea that built the field.

callout.text: The only valid way to be creative

storyboard.claim: Is inventing a whole profession the only valid way to create?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator frowning and thinking over the question.
storyboard.onScreenText: The only valid way to be creative
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the story into a question about everyone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the narrator's doubt on screen as a question, not a verdict.
storyboard.staging: Narrator worried and thinking: the question is a real worry.

storyboard.claim: A good designer at an agency is not a failure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator asking the question worriedly, as the listener would.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows the question to an ordinary job.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question on screen makes the fear explicit; the answer comes in the next beat.
storyboard.staging: Narrator pondering the fear of being a failure.

storyboard.claim: Society needs people who execute existing roles well.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An intact city: the structure society runs on.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from personal fear to the social order.
storyboard.addedInformation: The intact city shows the structure the narrator praises, not a critique of it.
storyboard.staging: Narrator talking beside an intact city: the stable order of ordinary jobs.

storyboard.claim: Big creative impact means shifting the whole culture.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target: the aim of a far-reaching goal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines the high goal the previous beat said is rare.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the 'capital C' impact a visible aim.
storyboard.staging: Narrator pointing at a target: the goal is to change the culture.

callout.text: Off the edge of the map

storyboard.claim: Creative impact steps off the edge of known territory, with no job title for it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An inventor standing at a ledge: stepping off into nothing.
storyboard.onScreenText: Off the edge of the map
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the target in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ledge makes the danger of having no existing role literal.
storyboard.staging: Inventor afraid at a ledge: he is stepping off the edge.

storyboard.claim: Expanding the domain forces the field to make new space for the person.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-step chain: expanding domain leads to new space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the ledge into a cause and effect.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the causal order the narrator states in one sentence.
storyboard.staging: Narrator talking over the chain: the domain expands, then space opens.

storyboard.claim: Why would anyone do this? The math is against you and rejection is brutal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An inventor slumped under the weight of rejection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Asks why anyone would take on this cost.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows the cost physically, the rejection named in the callout.
storyboard.staging: Inventor slumping, worried: rejection wears him down.

callout.text: Terrifying lack of a safety net

storyboard.claim: The hours are insane and there is no safety net.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A nervous young apprentice with wide eyes: a person with nothing to fall back on.
storyboard.onScreenText: Terrifying lack of a safety net
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the list of costs.
storyboard.addedInformation: A young face makes the missing safety net personal. No shield icon, which would read protection.
storyboard.staging: Apprentice afraid: the net is missing.

storyboard.claim: The reward is not fame or money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy with an apathetic face beside it: the prize does not move him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question why take the safe job.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blank face beside the trophy shows indifference. A plain trophy would read as fame.
storyboard.staging: Inventor blank beside a trophy: fame does not matter to him.

storyboard.claim: The real reward is flow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator naming the reward.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the positive answer after the strike.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the concept in plain words for the viewer.
storyboard.staging: Narrator talking: flow is the reward.

storyboard.claim: People do the work for the joy of the process itself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A man at a desk absorbed in a sheet of notes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains flow with a picture of someone doing it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes show the work itself as the reward. Sits in for the poet at his desk.
storyboard.staging: Inventor absorbed in his notes: he enjoys the work itself.

storyboard.claim: The world falls away in total immersion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same absorbed man, cut off from the room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the desk scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the state the picture already shows.
storyboard.staging: Inventor absorbed: the rest of the world has fallen away.

storyboard.claim: He loses all sense of time and does not think about lunch or the mortgage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The absorbed man at his desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens the immersion.
storyboard.addedInformation: No clock icon: it would read as a deadline. The callout carries the lost time.
storyboard.staging: Inventor thinking, absorbed: time has stopped for him.

storyboard.claim: Only the work exists: no past, no future.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The absorbed man, blank and still.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the immersion from inside.
storyboard.addedInformation: No hourglass, which would read as time running out.
storyboard.staging: Inventor blank and still: only the present work exists.

storyboard.claim: In that moment there is absolute uncertainty in his mind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worried man thinking through a problem.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the mental state of the immersion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Worried plus think reads as uncertainty; no icon for an abstract word.
storyboard.staging: Inventor worried and thinking: he is uncertain mid-work.

callout.text: If you rely on external rewards

storyboard.claim: If the creator depends on outside rewards, the creator will fail.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator talking directly to the listener.
storyboard.onScreenText: If you rely on external rewards
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the risk of outside rewards.
storyboard.addedInformation: No coin icon: a coin would read as endorsement of money.
storyboard.staging: Narrator talking to the listener: the warning is spoken, not shown.

storyboard.claim: Creators chasing money, fame or approval quit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor walking toward a door: leaving.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the warning of the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door reads as a way out, which is the quitting.
storyboard.staging: Inventor walking toward the door, worried: he is leaving the work.

storyboard.claim: Only 15 peers read a paper out of 7,000 submissions, so the rejection rate is too high for most egos.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An inventor slumped and sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why people quit.
storyboard.addedInformation: The numbers are in the callout. Stigler's name is not shown.
storyboard.staging: Inventor slumped and sad: the odds break him.

storyboard.claim: You must enjoy the frustrating struggle itself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor talking, calm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the answer to the rejection problem.
storyboard.addedInformation: No fighting pose: two people are needed for it to read as a fight.
storyboard.staging: Inventor talking calmly: the struggle is the reward.

storyboard.claim: A mathematician works all night on a grueling chromosome project.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator introducing the story.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the case story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the person; no bible cast member fits her, so the narrator tells it.
storyboard.staging: Narrator introducing the story: the case begins.

storyboard.claim: Her thought at dawn is not about being rich or famous.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator dismissing the reading.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the case story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the money and fame thought. Stages no coin or trophy, which would read as endorsement.
storyboard.staging: Narrator dismissing the money reading.

storyboard.claim: Flow is a state of perfect balance between high skill and high challenge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance: two sides in equilibrium.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the definition of flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: The balance icon reads as equal weight, matching skill against challenge.
storyboard.staging: Narrator talking beside a balance: skill and challenge meet.

storyboard.claim: When skill meets challenge, time distorts and self-consciousness vanishes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor thinking, absorbed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the definition of flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the vanishing self-doubt in the callout, not a symbol.
storyboard.staging: Inventor absorbed: the self has dropped away.

storyboard.claim: The narrator says he understands flow's psychology, then pivots.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator talking to the listener.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Marks the end of the flow explanation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Marks the turn to the objection.
storyboard.staging: Narrator talking: flow is understood, a pivot follows.

storyboard.claim: If the joy is purely personal, there is a contradiction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator thinking over the problem.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: No balance or crack icon: they would read as a verdict or a breakdown.
storyboard.staging: Narrator worried and thinking: a contradiction appears.

callout.text: Why fight for the Nobel Prize?

storyboard.claim: Creators fight for publication, the Nobel Prize and patrons' approval.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy: the Nobel Prize.
storyboard.onScreenText: Why fight for the Nobel Prize?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Asks why the internal joy is not enough.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trophy is the literal prize the narrator names.
storyboard.staging: Narrator talking beside a trophy: the external prize is the puzzle.

storyboard.claim: Flow in creative work comes from solving the puzzle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A game piece: the puzzle to solve.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the contradiction.
storyboard.addedInformation: The game icon reads as a puzzle with rules to solve.
storyboard.staging: Inventor thinking and happy: he is solving the puzzle.

storyboard.claim: Who decides what is correct, and how do you know you solved it?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The gatekeeper pointing: the one who decides.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows from solving the puzzle.
storyboard.addedInformation: The law icon reads as the rules that judge correctness.
storyboard.staging: Gatekeeper pointing with the law icon: the field decides.

storyboard.claim: You cannot trust yourself; the field validates against objective rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The gatekeeper pointing, skeptical.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers who decides.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout names the self-deception in the narrator's words.
storyboard.staging: Gatekeeper pointing: the field checks the self.

storyboard.claim: You cannot invent gibberish in a basement and experience flow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor talking, dismissive.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives a concrete example of the rejected path.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the private invention. No symbol.
storyboard.staging: Inventor talking: the private invention is rejected.

storyboard.claim: Flow requires proving your vision works in the external world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator pointing outward.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the external test.
storyboard.addedInformation: Points to the world outside the mind.
storyboard.staging: Narrator pointing out there: the vision must work in the world.

storyboard.claim: The narrator introduces a criticism of the systems view.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: No balance icon: it would read as a verdict on society.
storyboard.staging: Narrator talking: a criticism is coming.

callout.text: Push back hard on this premise

storyboard.claim: The narrator will push back hard on the premise.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator pointing at the premise.
storyboard.onScreenText: Push back hard on this premise
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the coming objection explicit.
storyboard.staging: Narrator pointing: the premise is challenged.

storyboard.claim: The systems model feels cold and strips away romance and soul.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the first objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: No heart icon: it would show romance, which the model removes.
storyboard.staging: Narrator talking: the model feels cold.

storyboard.claim: The model reduces passionate people to nodes in a machine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator, sad, talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the human cost of the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: No puppeteer icon: it would read as one person controlling others.
storyboard.staging: Narrator sad: people are reduced to parts.

storyboard.claim: Van Gogh's creative status depends on critics who decided decades after his death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave: the death the callout names.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Van Gogh.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grave icon shows the death; the painter stands for Van Gogh.
storyboard.staging: Painter sad beside a grave: recognition came after death.

storyboard.claim: His painting is meaningless without a gatekeeper's approval.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The painter alone with the gatekeeper and her clipboard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from death to the gatekeeper.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gatekeeper with clipboard shows the approval; the painter shows the isolation.
storyboard.staging: Painter sad, gatekeeper beside him: approval comes from outside.

storyboard.claim: The field sounds like a soulless dictatorship over expression.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer: one figure controlling others.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the critique as harsh.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry gatekeeper reads as threat; the puppeteer shows control.
storyboard.staging: Gatekeeper angry, pointing: the field is a controller.

callout.text: NOT CREATIVE UNTIL A GALLERY AGREES

storyboard.claim: The narrator rejects the claim that Van Gogh was not creative until a gallery approved him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The painter worried and thinking.
storyboard.onScreenText: Until a gallery said so (struck through)
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the reading just given.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the claim; no fake dismissive face.
storyboard.staging: Painter worried and thinking: the claim is rejected, not staged as true.
